title: Anthropic 拟感恩节前 IPO，接受低于预期的估值，募资 800–1000 亿美元
content:
The Decoder：AI News· Matthias Bastian·· 4 小时前精选AI 评分76
Anthropic 拟感恩节前 IPO，接受低于预期的估值，募资 800–1000 亿美元
Anthropic pushes ahead with pre-Thanksgiving IPO despite tech selloff, accepts lower valuation
AI 导读
据《金融时报》援引投资者的消息，Anthropic 计划在感恩节前 IPO，拟募资 800–1000 亿美元，估值 1.25–1.75 万亿美元，低于最乐观投资者期望的 2 万亿美元，但高于当前 9650 亿美元。
推荐理由
文中给出 Anthropic IPO 的估值区间、募资规模和最新的年化营收数字，可对照 OpenAI 融资动向看当前 AI 市场降温。
正文 · AI 翻译
2026年11月7日
尽管科技股遭遇抛售，Anthropic仍坚持推进IPO，并接受了较低的估值。据《金融时报》援引投资者的消息，这家Claude开发商希望在感恩节前上市，以1.25万亿至1.75万亿美元的估值融资800亿至1000亿美元。这一估值高于目前的9650亿美元，但低于最乐观投资者此前期待的2万亿美元。目前公布的年化营收约为810亿美元，高于7月底的约650亿美元。
借贷成本上升和庞大的AI支出计划引发了本周的科技股抛售。民主党赢得美国中期选举加速了这一跌势，因为他们曾承诺放缓数据中心建设等措施。纳斯达克100指数周四下跌6.4%，周五有所回升。
OpenAI也将其融资目标从1.4万亿美元下调至1.25万亿美元，并在最近仅筹集到最初寻求的300亿美元中的约三分之一。

report.summary: Anthropic is pushing ahead with a pre-Thanksgiving IPO at a $1.25–1.75 trillion valuation to raise $80–100 billion, accepting less than its most optimistic backers hoped amid a tech selloff.
report.background: Anthropic's listing lands at the end of a multi-year AI capital boom now colliding with higher borrowing costs. Labs and hyperscalers committed hundreds of billions of dollars to data centers, and investors increasingly demand demonstrated revenue rather than promised scale. The immediate trigger cited is a sharp tech selloff—the Nasdaq-100 fell 6.4% in a single session—accelerated by the Democratic midterm victory and pledges to slow data-center construction. That climate has already forced OpenAI to cut its fundraising target from $1.4 trillion to $1.25 trillion and to raise only about a third of the $30 billion it originally sought. Anthropic, riding Claude's enterprise traction and roughly $81 billion in annualized revenue, is opting to list anyway, taking a valuation haircut rather than waiting for sentiment to recover.
key_points: Anthropic wants to go public before Thanksgiving at a $1.25–1.75 trillion valuation, below the $2 trillion that optimistic investors had floated but well above its current $9.65 trillion... correction: above its current $965 billion mark. It is effectively trading headline valuation for deal certainty.

The company plans to raise $80–100 billion, an unusually large raise that would rank among the biggest IPOs ever and would give Anthropic a war chest to fund compute, model training and enterprise sales without returning to private markets.

Annualized revenue is reported at about $81 billion, up from roughly $65 billion at the end of July—around 25% growth in a single quarter. That trajectory is the core argument for the valuation and the main thing public investors will stress-test.

The backdrop is hostile: rising borrowing costs, sweeping AI spending plans and a 6.4% one-day Nasdaq-100 drop spooked markets. OpenAI's simultaneous downgrade—cutting its target to $1.25 trillion and raising only about a third of the $30 billion it sought—shows the whole sector repricing at once.

By proceeding rather than postponing, Anthropic signals it prefers public-market capital and liquidity now over holding out for a better multiple—a bet that being first to list at scale outweighs the cost of a discount.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is the first real public-market referendum on frontier-lab economics. A successful listing at a discount would establish a valuation anchor and force rivals—OpenAI, xAI, Mistral—to justify their private marks against audited revenue. A weak debut could freeze the IPO window and make late-stage private rounds harder. For developers, quarterly reporting means more disciplined API pricing, less aggressive subsidization and heavier emphasis on enterprise contracts, though platform stability and documentation may improve. For regular users, expect subscription tiers to be repriced toward profitability and consumer freebies to shrink as growth metrics become earnings metrics. The broader signal: AI is transitioning from a story about capability to a story about margins.
report.tools: To follow the story technically, watch Anthropic's open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP), now widely adopted for connecting models to tools; Claude Code and the Anthropic Cookbook for hands-on API examples; and its engineering blog on interpretability and safety. Developers hedging concentration risk should also evaluate open-weight alternatives—Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek—served via vLLM or Ollama, plus inference-cost trackers, so pricing changes after a listing don't catch you unprepared.
